title: Abnormal Psychology Adventure 2: Depression
welcome_lead: Today you'll explain depression from biological, cognitive and sociocultural angles.
meta_desc: Psychology Abnormal: depression — biological (serotonin), cognitive (Beck) and sociocultural explanations and CBT/SSRI.
final_note: You explained three approaches to depression and matched treatments.

concepts.def: Negative view of self, world, future

walkthroughs.body_html:
The monoamine hypothesis: low serotonin and noradrenaline cause depression.

Evidence: SSRIs (fluoxetine) increase serotonin and relieve symptoms in ~60% of cases.

Limits: Kirsch et al. (2008) meta-analysis questioned effect size vs placebo; mood lift lags days behind synaptic change.

Aaron Beck (1967): the cognitive triad — negative view of self, world and future.

Negative schemas activated by stress generate automatic negative thoughts.

Seligman (1967): learned helplessness from uncontrollable stress.

Treatment: CBT challenges negative thoughts and reinstates rewarding behaviour.

Brown & Harris (1978) found depression in women linked to chronic stressors (4+ children, no employment, no confidant).

Cultural factors: stigma in some cultures discourages help-seeking; somatic symptoms more prominent in some Asian cultures.
